content.text:
Submitted (validated, minimality ok).

**Repair made this round:** limb (d) was trimmed to the checklist boundary — the words "or the Research, Development, Manufacture or Commercialization of any SHP2 Inhibitor or Product in accordance with this Agreement" are gone. New 14.1(d) now reads:

> "(d) any allegation that the services performed or deliverables provided by RevMed under this Agreement or the RevMed Licensed Technology infringe or misappropriate the intellectual property rights of any Third Party; or (e) RevMed's breach of Applicable Law; or (f) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Sanofi's Confidential Information or other data of Sanofi caused by RevMed;"

This keeps the indemnity on RevMed's own supply side (element 3's services/deliverables trigger, mapped to this contract's licensed technology) instead of converting it into a freedom-to-operate indemnity over our downstream conduct, and it removes any tension with Article X's Product Infringement mechanics and the Profit/Loss Share Agreement.

**Confirmations requested by the verifier:**
- "RevMed Licensed Technology" is a defined term — Section 1.99 (RevMed Background Technology, RevMed Sole Program Technology and RevMed's half of Joint Program Technology).
- "Applicable Law" is defined at Section 1.8; "Third Party Claims" at 1.126; "Confidential Information" at 1.21.
- 14.1(b) (RevMed's material breach of warranties/representations) is untouched and retained in full, so the "((a) through (f))" range covers a continuous, existing lettering sequence.
- Section 13.5 is unaffected: 14.1(d) allocates third-party claims rather than granting a warranty, which is the point to make if RevMed pushes back.

Unchanged: the narrowing of 14.2 to Sanofi-provided content and Sanofi's breach of Applicable Law, the "[Intentionally omitted]" placeholders preserving 14.2's lettering, and the untouched 14.3 notice/control/cooperation machinery. Preferred level; all ten elements mapped once.
